title: Chip anatomy
head:
Chip anatomy
A chip is laid out like a card: name and kind on the left, marks on the right (▶ presentations, then the kind's pill or badge), counts below. Where a card shows its table, a chip shows a well: what it holds, as a quiet treemap, named where there is room.
Holds parts: the strongest fill and border; its well is a plain recess. A diagram: a middle fill; its well is framed in its hue like a small canvas, its kind on a tab at the frame's right. Both lay their children by weight, never by the diagram's own arrangement, and draw no lines.
Too short for a well: a diagram carries its kind as a pill on the right of its name. A leaf: quiet fill, a hollow badge, nothing inside. An actor: no fill, a round outline in its hue. An external: no fill, a dashed outline, its name muted. A closed folder or package: neutral, holding its parts like any holder.
